task.description:
Close ISS-0439 per WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5's procedure. This run's own job (RECORDING the deferral decision and its reasoning durably, per this issue's own six acceptance criteria) is now complete and independently gated PASS by both CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step 2) and REVIEWER (step 3) -- the underlying FEATURE QUESTION (should Letflow adopt the 1C taxonomy) remains genuinely deferred/unbuilt, and that is the correct, intended outcome, not a partial result.

Determine which terminal status applies, per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'Issue status vocabulary' section (read it in full before choosing) -- do not default to 'resolved' without checking the definition. This run DID actually remove something ISS-0439 named as its defect: the issue's own filed problem was 'this decision and its reasoning are not durably recorded anywhere a future reader would find them' (its six ACs are entirely about recording, not about the taxonomy question itself) -- and that recording gap is now genuinely closed: a decision record exists, gated, at docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md, plus a grounding artefact. Since a root cause (the gap) was actually removed and is durably in place (not merely diagnosed), 'resolved' is the status that matches ISS_QUEUE.md's own definition -- but verify this reasoning against the vocabulary yourself rather than taking it as given; if you disagree after reading the definitions, state why and use the status you conclude is correct instead.

Set docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml: status: resolved (or your own concluded status), resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0439-20260904, resolved_at: <real UTC timestamp>, and a resolution: field stating plainly that the deferral itself is unchanged -- what closed is the tracking/recording gap this issue exists to fix, not the underlying product question, which remains open per the review triggers named in decision 0019.

Then close GitHub issue #846 per this project's evidence-on-close rule (ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'Closing an issue's GitHub mirror' section and WF-03 Step 5's own comment-branching text) -- this MUST carry a --comment citing the resolving evidence (this run-id, the docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml record, and the decision record path) since there is no regression test to cite (this issue produces no code). Be honest in the comment that the underlying feature question (1C taxonomy adoption) remains deferred/unbuilt -- this run resolves the tracking/recording gap only, per this issue's own six ACs, which were entirely about recording, not about building the feature.

Do NOT call letflow-queue yourself (release_lock is ORCH-only, per TASK_QUEUE.md's 'who calls what' -- ORCH will call it in the same turn as this step's PASS, per WF-03 Step 5's own instruction to ORCH).
acceptance_criteria: docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml's status field is flipped to a terminal value chosen by reading ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary definitions, not assumed, with the correct paired keys for whichever status is chosen (resolved_in_run:/resolved_at: for 'resolved'; a different key pair for 'instrumented'/'no_defect' if either of those is concluded instead)
The resolution/verdict text states plainly that the underlying 1C-taxonomy-adoption question remains deferred/unbuilt -- this run closes the recording gap, not the feature question

GitHub issue #846 is closed with a --comment citing the run-id, the docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml record path, and the decision record path (docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md) -- never a bare close with no comment
The close comment does not claim a fix was shipped or a regression test exists (neither applies to this issue)
docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml is committed to git as part of this step
